description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Ubuntu 22.04 for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters. For reference, you can find this notification in the Azure portal under Service Health/Health advisories using tracking ID: 9Y2Z-_K8. On 30 June 2027, we'll retire Ubuntu 22.04 on Azure Kubernetes Service. To avoid disruptions, transition to Ubuntu 24.04 or later by that date. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/upgrade-os-version) (https://aka.ms/aks/supported-ubuntu-versions)Newer supported versions include kernel updates and security improvements (https://discourse.ubuntu.com/t/ubuntu-24-04-lts-noble-numbat-release-notes/39890). Between now and 30 June 2027, you can continue to use Ubuntu 22.04 on AKS without disruption. If you don't migrate by 30 June 2027, you won't be able to create new node pools, AKS won't produce new node images, and you'll no longer receive security patches for existing node pools. If you'd like to enable long-term support with Kubernetes version 1.33 or later, first update your node pools to Ubuntu 24.04. Additionally, on 30 April 2028 AKS will remove Ubuntu 22.04 node images and existing code, causing scaling and remediation operations to fail. Recommended action To avoid service disruptions such as security vulnerabilities, failed node image upgrades, and scaling failures, migrate to Ubuntu 24.04 or later by 30 June 2027. (https://aka.ms/aks/upgrade-os-version)Your migration options include: Default Operating System SKU (OSSku): If you're using 'Ubuntu,' you'll automatically migrate to Ubuntu 24.04 when you upgrade your Kubernetes version to 1.35 or later. Versioned OSSku: If you're using 'Ubuntu2204,' update your OSSku to 'Ubuntu' for Kubernetes 1.35 or later, or 'Ubuntu2404' for Kubernetes 1.32 or later. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://learn.microsoft.com/answers/tags/200/azure-kubernetes-service) or AKS GitHub. If you have a support plan and need technical help, follow our documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-portal/supportability/how-to-create-azure-support-request#open-a-support-request-from-the-global-header) to create a support request. short_description_solution: Action required: Migrate your legacy Azure general-purpose v1 account to a general-purpose v2 account
summary: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that have a legacy blob storage account.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that have a legacy blob storage account. On 13 October 2026, we'll retire blob-only storage accounts. To avoid disruptions, migrate your GPv1 storage accounts to GPv2 accounts before that date (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/legacy-blob-storage-account-migration-overview). GPv2 accounts give you access to the latest Azure Storage features while providing improved performance and true zonal redundancy support. Required action To avoid service disruptions, migrate your GPv1 storage accounts to GPv2 by 13 October 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/legacy-blob-storage-account-migration-overview). To view your impacted resources in the Azure portal, go to the Storage Center (https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_StorageHub/StorageHub.MenuView/~/StorageAccountsBrowse) and look for Kind: Storage. For Azure Databricks managed storage accounts: If your workspace relies on a GPv1 storage account, you won't be able to migrate that account manually. As part of this retirement, Microsoft will schedule and complete a managed migration of affected accounts to GPv2 on your behalf; no action is required. Azure Databricks accounts will not be part of this migration and will be done separately. When Azure Databricks account migration is planned, notifications will be sent as appropriate. Any non-Azure Databricks accounts that use GPv1 will require manual migration. Automatic migration warning After 13 October 2026, all existing legacy blob storage accounts will be automatically migrated over to a GPv2 account, which may result in higher billing costs. Your decision not to migrate an existing legacy blob storage account will be construed as consent for Microsoft to migrate the account on your behalf. Creation of all new GPv1 accounts will be blocked by 13 October 2026. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://learn.microsoft.com/answers/tags/125/azure-blob-storage). If you have a support plan and need technical help, open the Azure portal (https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/HelpAndSupportBlade/overview) and select the question mark icon at the top of the page. Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook (https://aka.ms/ServicesRetirementWorkbook). Please note that retirements may not be visible in the workbook for up to two weeks after being announced.

If you don't migrate by 30 June 2027, you won't be able to create new node pools, AKS won't produce new node images, and you'll no longer receive security patches for existing node pools. If you'd like to enable long-term support with Kubernetes version 1.33 or later, first update your node pools to Ubuntu 24.04. Additionally, on 30 April 2028 AKS will remove Ubuntu 22.04 node images and existing code, causing scaling and remediation operations to fail. Recommended action To avoid service disruptions such as security vulnerabilities, failed node image upgrades, and scaling failures, migrate to Ubuntu 24.04 or later by 30 June 2027. summary: You’re receiving this notification because you’re associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Ubuntu 22.04 for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters. For reference, you can find this notification in the Azure portal under Service Health/Health advisories using tracking ID: 9Y2Z-_K8.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Ubuntu 22.04 for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters. For reference, you can find this notification in the Azure portal under Service Health/Health advisories using tracking ID: 9Y2Z-_K8. On 30 June 2027, we'll retire Ubuntu 22.04 on Azure Kubernetes Service. To avoid disruptions, transition to Ubuntu 24.04 or later by that date. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/upgrade-os-version) (https://aka.ms/aks/supported-ubuntu-versions)Newer supported versions include kernel updates and security improvements (https://discourse.ubuntu.com/t/ubuntu-24-04-lts-noble-numbat-release-notes/39890). Between now and 30 June 2027, you can continue to use Ubuntu 22.04 on AKS without disruption. If you don't migrate by 30 June 2027, you won't be able to create new node pools, AKS won't produce new node images, and you'll no longer receive security patches for existing node pools. If you'd like to enable long-term support with Kubernetes version 1.33 or later, first update your node pools to Ubuntu 24.04. Additionally, on 30 April 2028 AKS will remove Ubuntu 22.04 node images and existing code, causing scaling and remediation operations to fail. Recommended action To avoid service disruptions such as security vulnerabilities, failed node image upgrades, and scaling failures, migrate to Ubuntu 24.04 or later by 30 June 2027. (https://aka.ms/aks/upgrade-os-version)Your migration options include: Default Operating System SKU (OSSku): If you're using 'Ubuntu,' you'll automatically migrate to Ubuntu 24.04 when you upgrade your Kubernetes version to 1.35 or later. Versioned OSSku: If you're using 'Ubuntu2204,' update your OSSku to 'Ubuntu' for Kubernetes 1.35 or later, or 'Ubuntu2404' for Kubernetes 1.32 or later. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://learn.microsoft.com/answers/tags/200/azure-kubernetes-service) or AKS GitHub. If you have a support plan and need technical help, follow our documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-portal/supportability/how-to-create-azure-support-request#open-a-support-request-from-the-global-header) to create a support request. Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook (https://aka.ms/ServicesRetirementWorkbook). Please note that retirements may not be visible in the workbook for up to two weeks after being announced.

short_description_solution: Action required: Validate Java TLS compatibility before App Service JDK security updates (starting 20 October 2026)
summary: You’re receiving this notification because one or more of your Azure subscriptions use Java workloads on Azure App Service.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because one or more of your Azure subscriptions use Java workloads on Azure App Service. Starting on 20 October 2026 (phased rollout), App Service Java runtimes may begin updating to JDK 11.0.30+, 17.0.18+, and 21.0.10+ (and later patch versions) during region-specific maintenance windows/non-business hours. In these JDK versions: SHA-1 is disabled for TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2 handshake signatures. TLS_RSA cipher suites are disabled by default. These changes improve security by removing legacy cryptographic algorithms, but they can cause compatibility issues with older endpoints or dependencies. For production workloads, Microsoft guidance remains to use pinned patch JVM versions to reduce unanticipated outages from patch auto-update: Deploy and Configure Tomcat, JBoss EAP, or Java SE Apps - Azure App Service | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/configure-language-java-deploy-run?tabs=windows&pivot%E2%80%A6) Potential impact Applications that depend on legacy TLS settings may experience connection failures, commonly seen as SSLHandshakeException in application logs (often not platform logs), including: "No appropriate protocol (protocol is disabled or cipher suites are inappropriate)"This usually indicates the remote endpoint only supports TLSRSA cipher suites. "No supported signature algorithm..."This usually indicates the remote endpoint signs TLS 1.2 handshakes with SHA-1. Action required 1.Identify impacted connections. Review application logs for SSLHandshakeException. Audit dependencies/endpoints for SHA-1 handshake signatures or TLSRSA-only cipher support. 2.Remediate incompatible dependencies. Update endpoints/libraries to support modern cryptographic settings, such as SHA-256+ signatures and stronger cipher suites. 3.Validate in pre-production. Test compatibility before rollout. For testing environments, set Platform Release Setting to "latest" so runtime changes are exercised early. 4.Use temporary mitigation if needed for production continuity. If remediation cannot complete before rollout, consider pinning to a known-good Java patch version as a short-term mitigation. Track and remove this mitigation once dependencies are updated. 5.Override Java security settings only as a last resort (not recommended long-term). This can reduce cryptographic security posture and should be time-boxed. Create a file named security-override.properties in your site directory (example path shown below): # D:\home\site\security-override.properties jdk.tls.disabledAlgorithms=SSLv3, TLSv1, TLSv1.1, DTLSv1.0, RC4, DES, MD5withRSA, DH keySize less than 1024, EC keySize less than 224, 3DESEDECBC, anon, NULL Then add the following JVM argument to your app's JAVAOPTS: -Djava.security.properties=D:\home\site\security-override.properties Important: Treat this override as temporary. Plan removal after endpoint/dependency remediation. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://learn.microsoft.com/answers/tags/20/azure-monitor). If you have a support plan and need technical help, please submit a support request (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-portal/supportability/how-to-create-azure-support-request). If you have additional questions, please contact us at java-core@microsoft.com Account Information {% for item in items %} Subscription ID: {{ item.subscriptionId }} Subscription name: {{ item.subscriptionName }} {% endfor %}

short_description_solution: Action required: Verify your OS compatibility with Microsoft Azure Network Adapter (MANA) hardware for Intel D- and E- v5-series VMs and Cobalt 100 D- and E- v6-series VM
summary: You are receiving this notification because you are running one or more Azure virtual machines that may be affected by an upcoming infrastructure change.
description_problem: You are receiving this notification because you are running one or more Azure virtual machines that may be affected by an upcoming infrastructure change. As previously communicated on 29 May 2026, Azure has begun a staged roll out of the following virtual machines (VMs) on Microsoft Azure Network Adapter (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-overview)-enabled hardware: Intel: Dsv5, Dv5, Ddsv5, Ddv5, Dlsv5, Dldsv5, Esv5, Ev5, Edsv5, Edv5 Cobalt 100: Dpsv6, Dpdsv6, Dplsv6, Dpldsv6, Epsv6, Epdsv6 If accelerated networking is not being used or if you are already running a supported Windows or Linux OS version (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-overview?tabs=NetworkManager) on these VMs, no further action is required. The regions already enabled for these VMs on MANA-capable hardware are: West Central US, East Asia, Norway West, Spain Central. This update is announcing additional regional deployments of MANA-capable hardware for the VMs above: 29 June 2026: UK South, US Central, US East 30 June 2026: US North, US South, Europe West 6 July 2026: US East 2, US West 2, and all remaining public regions If you're running VM series listed above using Accelerated Networking, any new VM deployments or existing VMs which are redeployed due to maintenance events or customer action may land on MANA-enabled hardware once live in your region. If your VMs are running Network Virtual Appliance (NVA) workloads, you'll need to verify that they are compatible with MANA-enabled hardware in your region(s). Some NVA and high network concurrency workloads may see performance degradation if not running on an OS with the MANA driver. Most other types of workloads are expected to run without performance degradation using an alternate netvsc networking path. Action required Verify that your workloads are compatible with MANA-enabled hardware by following the steps below: Identify all Intel D- and E- v5-series and Cobalt 100 D- and E- v6-series VMs using Accelerated Networking running NVA workloads. Verify your OS is MANA compatible. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-linux) If your OS isn't MANA compatible, upgrade to an OS or NVA product that is. Contact your NVA provider for a list of MANA compatible products. If you have NVA workloads and need additional time to complete step 3 (MANA Compatibility), you can establish a temporary MANA exception by applying and enabling the "LegacyVMNVA" tag (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-network-virtual-appliance-opt-out#temporary-mana-exception-with-legacyvmnva). This step can be done at any time up until the tag expiration date of 31 May 2027. If the "LegacyVMNVA" tag isn't applied and enabled before your region has the MANA-enabled hardware, your VMs may be deployed on that hardware. Upgrade to a MANA compatible OS or NVA product by 31 May 2027. After that date, the tag will no longer be valid and any VM could land on MANA-enabled hardware. If you continue using the above VMs without MANA compatibility, they'll remain supported on both existing Mellanox and new MANAenabled hardware until the size is retired. Help and support If you have questions or run into any issues, please contact your Customer Support Account Manager (CSAM), if available, or reach out to Support (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-machines/vm-support-help) for assistance. The following resources are available to support you: Landing page: Legacy VMs on MANA Rollout (https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/teams/AzureReliabilityPortal/SitePages/Legacy-VMs-on-MANA-Rollout.aspx?TeamsCID=dd6d9562-c6a9-4756-ac58-62a1fb7fe900&OR=Teams-HL&CT=1781881120544&linkOpenTime=1782158414535&isSPOFile=1&&sdata=WUZ5YzNpcitvTDZzblgxWWFjMldjUW1LaDV1akV0UnJ2RjNNZEkxWWwzaz0=&ovuser=72f988bf-86f1-41af-91ab-2d7cd011db47%2Canreicha@microsoft.com&clickparams=eyJBcHBOYW1lIjoiVGVhbXMtRGVza3RvcCIsIkFwcFZlcnNpb24iOiI0OS8yNjA1MjkwNjExOCJ9) Microsoft Azure Network Adapter overview (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-overview) MANA support for existing VM sizes (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-existing-sizes) MANA support for Network Virtual Appliances (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-network-virtual-appliance-opt-out) Windows VMs with the Microsoft Azure Network Adapter (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-windows#verify-that-traffic-is-flowing-through-mana) Support (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-machines/vm-support-help)

summary: We recently sent you an email regarding Azure Synapse Link for Azure Cosmos DB (NoSQL). description_problem: We recently sent you an email regarding Azure Synapse Link for Azure Cosmos DB (NoSQL). We sincerely apologize that the previous communication did not include the required account details, specifically the resourceGroupName and databaseAccountName. This follow-up email includes the missing information. We regret any confusion or inconvenience this may have caused and appreciate your understanding. ----------------------------------------------------- You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that currently use Azure Synapse Link for Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL. For reference, you can find this notification in the Azure portal under Service Health/Health advisories (https://aka.ms/AzureServiceHealthAdvisories) using tracking ID: 9JYQ-GL0. Azure Synapse Link for Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL will be retired on 31 March 2029, transition to Cosmos DB Mirroring in Microsoft Fabric (https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/mirroring/azure-cosmos-db) by that date or, if you are not using the analytical capabilities, disable Azure Synapse Link on those accounts using our provided script (https://github.com/AzureCosmosDB/cosmos-fabric-samples/tree/main/disable-synapse-link). Cosmos DB Mirroring in Microsoft Fabric is the supported successor for Synapse Link's analytical scenarios. On 31 March 2029, workloads running Azure Synapse Link for Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL will face disruptions to their analytical workloads as they will no longer have access to the Analytical Store. If your account has any historical data in your Analytical Store that exceeds your transactional retention window, that data will no longer be accessible after retirement. Resources to aid in your migration can be found below. Action recommended Disable Synapse Link for Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL on your accounts before 31 March 2029. Use our script (https://github.com/AzureCosmosDB/cosmos-fabric-samples/tree/main/disable-synapse-link) to identify and disable affected containers. Caution: Disabling is irreversible. Disabling Synapse Link removes your Analytical Store data permanently. If you have analytical workloads running against the Analytical Store, or if you use the Analytical Store to retain historical data beyond your transactional TTL, migrate to Cosmos DB Mirroring (https://aka.ms/CosmosMirrorSynapseMigration) first. If you are unsure whether you have analytical data, check out your Synapse workspace before disabling. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://learn.microsoft.com/answers/tags/187/azure-cosmos-db/). If you have a support plan and need technical help, create a support request (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-portal/supportability/how-to-create-azure-support-request). Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook (https://aka.ms/ServicesRetirementWorkbook). short_description_solution: Retirement notice: We're improving the high availability experience for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
summary: You’re receiving this notification because you’re associated with one or more Azure subscriptions with Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server instances. For reference, you can find this notification in the Azure portal under Service Health/Health advisories using tracking ID: ZPDZ-SL8.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions with Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server instances. For reference, you can find this notification in the Azure portal under Service Health/Health advisories (https://aka.ms/AzureServiceHealthAdvisories) using tracking ID: ZPDZ-SL8. We've rolled out improvements to the high availability experience for Azure Database for PostgreSQL to simplify configuration and strengthen long-term resiliency against zonal failures. What's changing With this experience enabled in the Azure portal and Azure CLI, Azure will now default to zone-redundant high availability. If the selected region doesn't support that, you can choose a fallback mechanism (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/postgresql/high-availability/concepts-high-availability#configure-business-critical-high-availability-options) by selecting the fallback checkbox in the Azure portal or by using the allow-same-zone parameter in the Azure CLI. Changes in the Azure portal include: High availability is now labelled business critical (high availability). If you previously had the experience enabled, no action is required from you. A new zonal resiliency option is available. When enabled, Azure deploys a standby server in a different availability zone from the primary one, helping protect workloads from zonal outages. Automatic migration notice Automatic migration will be supported for new servers created after 12 February 2026 as soon as regional capacity is available. Servers created before 12 February 2026 will be automatically migrated over time. You won't need to redeploy or make configuration changes. From 1 September 2026, servers created using same-zone high availability via developer tools including Terraform, Bicep, SDKs (.NET, Python, Java, JavaScript, and Go), PowerShell, and Ansible will be automatically migrated once capacity becomes available in the region. After the transition, writes are committed across multiple availability zones. This may result in minor changes in write behaviour, with minimal latency impact and improved resiliency and durability. If you'd like to migrate sooner, self-service migration options, such as point-in-time restore or read replicas, will allow you to move to a zone-redundant configuration at your own pace. Read our documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/postgresql/high-availability/how-to-configure-high-availability?tabs=portal-enable-existing-server%2Cportal-disable-existing-server%2Cportal-enable-new-server%2Cportal-forced-failover%2Cportal-planned-failover#limitations-and-considerations) to learn more about self-service migration options, zonal resiliency, the built-in fallback capability, and automatic migration behaviour. Help and support If you have questions about how these changes apply to your deployments or automation workflows, please reach out to us through Microsoft support, your account team, or the feedback forum. (https://feedback.azure.com/d365community/forum/c5e32b97-ee24-ec11-b6e6-000d3a4f0da0) If you have general questions, ask community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://learn.microsoft.com/answers/tags/214/azure-database-postgresql). If you have a support plan and you need technical help, open the Azure portal (https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/HelpAndSupportBlade/newsupportrequest) and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.

description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Ubuntu 22.04 for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters. For reference, you can find this notification in the Azure portal under Service Health/Health advisories using tracking ID: 9Y2Z-_K8. On 30 June 2027, we'll retire Ubuntu 22.04 on Azure Kubernetes Service. To avoid disruptions, transition to Ubuntu 24.04 or later by that date. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/upgrade-os-version) (https://aka.ms/aks/supported-ubuntu-versions)Newer supported versions include kernel updates and security improvements (https://discourse.ubuntu.com/t/ubuntu-24-04-lts-noble-numbat-release-notes/39890). Between now and 30 June 2027, you can continue to use Ubuntu 22.04 on AKS without disruption. If you don't migrate by 30 June 2027, you won't be able to create new node pools, AKS won't produce new node images, and you'll no longer receive security patches for existing node pools. If you'd like to enable long-term support with Kubernetes version 1.33 or later, first update your node pools to Ubuntu 24.04. Additionally, on 30 April 2028 AKS will remove Ubuntu 22.04 node images and existing code, causing scaling and remediation operations to fail. Recommended action To avoid service disruptions such as security vulnerabilities, failed node image upgrades, and scaling failures, migrate to Ubuntu 24.04 or later by 30 June 2027. (https://aka.ms/aks/upgrade-os-version)Your migration options include: Default Operating System SKU (OSSku): If you're using 'Ubuntu,' you'll automatically migrate to Ubuntu 24.04 when you upgrade your Kubernetes version to 1.35 or later. Versioned OSSku: If you're using 'Ubuntu2204,' update your OSSku to 'Ubuntu' for Kubernetes 1.35 or later, or 'Ubuntu2404' for Kubernetes 1.32 or later. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://learn.microsoft.com/answers/tags/200/azure-kubernetes-service) or AKS GitHub. If you have a support plan and need technical help, follow our documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-portal/supportability/how-to-create-azure-support-request#open-a-support-request-from-the-global-header) to create a support request. Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook (https://aka.ms/ServicesRetirementWorkbook). Please note that retirements may not be visible in the workbook for up to two weeks after being announced.

short_description_solution: Action required: Validate Java TLS compatibility before App Service JDK security updates (starting 20 October 2026)
summary: You’re receiving this notification because one or more of your Azure subscriptions use Java workloads on Azure App Service.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because one or more of your Azure subscriptions use Java workloads on Azure App Service. Starting on 20 October 2026 (phased rollout), App Service Java runtimes may begin updating to JDK 11.0.30+, 17.0.18+, and 21.0.10+ (and later patch versions) during region-specific maintenance windows/non-business hours. In these JDK versions: SHA-1 is disabled for TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2 handshake signatures. TLS_RSA cipher suites are disabled by default. These changes improve security by removing legacy cryptographic algorithms, but they can cause compatibility issues with older endpoints or dependencies. For production workloads, Microsoft guidance remains to use pinned patch JVM versions to reduce unanticipated outages from patch auto-update: Deploy and Configure Tomcat, JBoss EAP, or Java SE Apps - Azure App Service | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/configure-language-java-deploy-run?tabs=windows&pivot%E2%80%A6) Potential impact Applications that depend on legacy TLS settings may experience connection failures, commonly seen as SSLHandshakeException in application logs (often not platform logs), including: "No appropriate protocol (protocol is disabled or cipher suites are inappropriate)"This usually indicates the remote endpoint only supports TLSRSA cipher suites. "No supported signature algorithm..."This usually indicates the remote endpoint signs TLS 1.2 handshakes with SHA-1. Action required 1.Identify impacted connections. Review application logs for SSLHandshakeException. Audit dependencies/endpoints for SHA-1 handshake signatures or TLSRSA-only cipher support. 2.Remediate incompatible dependencies. Update endpoints/libraries to support modern cryptographic settings, such as SHA-256+ signatures and stronger cipher suites. 3.Validate in pre-production. Test compatibility before rollout. summary: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that have a GPv1 storage account. For reference, you can find this health advisory notification in the Azure portal using tracking ID: XTKT-BW8.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that have a GPv1 storage account. For reference, you can find this health advisory notification in the Azure portal (https://aka.ms/AzureServiceHealthAdvisories) using tracking ID: XTKT-BW8. From 1 September 2026 the creation of new GPv1 accounts will be blocked, the creation of GPv2 accounts will be unaffected. On 13 October 2026, we'll retire GPv1 storage accounts. To avoid disruptions, migrate your GPv1 storage accounts to GPv2 accounts before that date (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-account-upgrade?tabs=azure-portal). GPv2 accounts give you access to the latest Azure Storage features while providing improved performance and true zonal redundancy support. Recommended action To avoid service disruptions, migrate your GPv1 storage accounts to GPv2 by 13 October 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-account-upgrade?tabs=azure-portal). To view your impacted resources in the Azure portal, go to the Storage Center (https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_StorageHub/StorageHub.MenuView/~/StorageAccountsBrowse)and look for Kind: Storage. For additional ways to access impacted resource information, see this documentation (https://aka.ms/AzureRetirementImpactedResourcesChannels). Watch the recorded video and demo here (https://aka.ms/GPv1RetirementLiveStream). Frequently asked questions are available in the documentation. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/general-purpose-version-1-account-migration-frequently-asked-questions) For Azure Databricks managed storage accounts: If your workspace relies on a GPv1 storage account, you won't be able to migrate that account manually. As part of this retirement, Microsoft will schedule and complete a managed migration of affected accounts to GPv2 on your behalf; no action is required. Azure Databricks accounts will not be part of this migration and will be done separately. When Azure Databricks account migration is planned, notifications will be sent as appropriate. Any non-Azure Databricks accounts that use GPv1 will require manual migration. Automatic migration warning After 13 October 2026, all existing GPv1 storage accounts will be automatically migrated over to a GPv2 account, which may result in higher billing costs. Your decision not to migrate an existing GPv1 storage account will be construed as consent for Microsoft to migrate the account on your behalf. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. (https://learn.microsoft.com/answers/tags/125/azure-blob-storage) If you have a support plan and need technical help, open the Azure portal (https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/HelpAndSupportBlade/overview) and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.

summary: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that have a GPv1 storage account. For reference, you can find this health advisory notification in the Azure portal using tracking ID: XTKT-BW8.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that have a GPv1 storage account. For reference, you can find this health advisory notification in the Azure portal (https://aka.ms/AzureServiceHealthAdvisories) using tracking ID: XTKT-BW8. From 1 September 2026 the creation of new GPv1 accounts will be blocked, the creation of GPv2 accounts will be unaffected. On 13 October 2026, we'll retire GPv1 storage accounts. To avoid disruptions, migrate your GPv1 storage accounts to GPv2 accounts before that date (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-account-upgrade?tabs=azure-portal). GPv2 accounts give you access to the latest Azure Storage features while providing improved performance and true zonal redundancy support. Recommended action To avoid service disruptions, migrate your GPv1 storage accounts to GPv2 by 13 October 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-account-upgrade?tabs=azure-portal). To view your impacted resources in the Azure portal, go to the Storage Center (https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_StorageHub/StorageHub.MenuView/~/StorageAccountsBrowse)and look for Kind: Storage. For additional ways to access impacted resource information, see this documentation (https://aka.ms/AzureRetirementImpactedResourcesChannels). Watch the recorded video and demo here (https://aka.ms/GPv1RetirementLiveStream). Frequently asked questions are available in the documentation. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/general-purpose-version-1-account-migration-frequently-asked-questions) For Azure Databricks managed storage accounts: If your workspace relies on a GPv1 storage account, you won't be able to migrate that account manually. As part of this retirement, Microsoft will schedule and complete a managed migration of affected accounts to GPv2 on your behalf; no action is required. Azure Databricks accounts will not be part of this migration and will be done separately. When Azure Databricks account migration is planned, notifications will be sent as appropriate. Any non-Azure Databricks accounts that use GPv1 will require manual migration. Automatic migration warning After 13 October 2026, all existing GPv1 storage accounts will be automatically migrated over to a GPv2 account, which may result in higher billing costs. Your decision not to migrate an existing GPv1 storage account will be construed as consent for Microsoft to migrate the account on your behalf. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. (https://learn.microsoft.com/answers/tags/125/azure-blob-storage) If you have a support plan and need technical help, open the Azure portal (https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/HelpAndSupportBlade/overview) and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.

short_description_solution: Action required: Verify your OS compatibility with Microsoft Azure Network Adapter (MANA) hardware for Intel D- and E- v5-series VMs and Cobalt 100 D- and E- v6-series VM
summary: You are receiving this notification because you are running one or more Azure virtual machines that may be affected by an upcoming infrastructure change.
description_problem: You are receiving this notification because you are running one or more Azure virtual machines that may be affected by an upcoming infrastructure change. As previously communicated on 29 May 2026, Azure has begun a staged roll out of the following virtual machines (VMs) on Microsoft Azure Network Adapter (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-overview)-enabled hardware: Intel: Dsv5, Dv5, Ddsv5, Ddv5, Dlsv5, Dldsv5, Esv5, Ev5, Edsv5, Edv5 Cobalt 100: Dpsv6, Dpdsv6, Dplsv6, Dpldsv6, Epsv6, Epdsv6 If accelerated networking is not being used or if you are already running a supported Windows or Linux OS version (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-overview?tabs=NetworkManager) on these VMs, no further action is required. The regions already enabled for these VMs on MANA-capable hardware are: West Central US, East Asia, Norway West, Spain Central. This update is announcing additional regional deployments of MANA-capable hardware for the VMs above: 29 June 2026: UK South, US Central, US East 30 June 2026: US North, US South, Europe West 6 July 2026: US East 2, US West 2, and all remaining public regions If you're running VM series listed above using Accelerated Networking, any new VM deployments or existing VMs which are redeployed due to maintenance events or customer action may land on MANA-enabled hardware once live in your region. If your VMs are running Network Virtual Appliance (NVA) workloads, you'll need to verify that they are compatible with MANA-enabled hardware in your region(s). Some NVA and high network concurrency workloads may see performance degradation if not running on an OS with the MANA driver. Most other types of workloads are expected to run without performance degradation using an alternate netvsc networking path. Action required Verify that your workloads are compatible with MANA-enabled hardware by following the steps below: Identify all Intel D- and E- v5-series and Cobalt 100 D- and E- v6-series VMs using Accelerated Networking running NVA workloads. Verify your OS is MANA compatible. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-linux) If your OS isn't MANA compatible, upgrade to an OS or NVA product that is. Contact your NVA provider for a list of MANA compatible products. If you have NVA workloads and need additional time to complete step 3 (MANA Compatibility), you can establish a temporary MANA exception by applying and enabling the "LegacyVMNVA" tag (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-network-virtual-appliance-opt-out#temporary-mana-exception-with-legacyvmnva). This step can be done at any time up until the tag expiration date of 31 May 2027. If the "LegacyVMNVA" tag isn't applied and enabled before your region has the MANA-enabled hardware, your VMs may be deployed on that hardware. Upgrade to a MANA compatible OS or NVA product by 31 May 2027. After that date, the tag will no longer be valid and any VM could land on MANA-enabled hardware. If you continue using the above VMs without MANA compatibility, they'll remain supported on both existing Mellanox and new MANAenabled hardware until the size is retired. Help and support If you have questions or run into any issues, please contact your Customer Support Account Manager (CSAM), if available, or reach out to Support (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-machines/vm-support-help) for assistance. summary: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that have a GPv1 storage account. For reference, you can find this health advisory notification in the Azure portal using tracking ID: XTKT-BW8.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that have a GPv1 storage account. For reference, you can find this health advisory notification in the Azure portal (https://aka.ms/AzureServiceHealthAdvisories) using tracking ID: XTKT-BW8. From 1 September 2026 the creation of new GPv1 accounts will be blocked, the creation of GPv2 accounts will be unaffected. On 13 October 2026, we'll retire GPv1 storage accounts. To avoid disruptions, migrate your GPv1 storage accounts to GPv2 accounts before that date (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-account-upgrade?tabs=azure-portal). GPv2 accounts give you access to the latest Azure Storage features while providing improved performance and true zonal redundancy support. Recommended action To avoid service disruptions, migrate your GPv1 storage accounts to GPv2 by 13 October 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-account-upgrade?tabs=azure-portal). To view your impacted resources in the Azure portal, go to the Storage Center (https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_StorageHub/StorageHub.MenuView/~/StorageAccountsBrowse)and look for Kind: Storage. For additional ways to access impacted resource information, see this documentation (https://aka.ms/AzureRetirementImpactedResourcesChannels). Watch the recorded video and demo here (https://aka.ms/GPv1RetirementLiveStream). Frequently asked questions are available in the documentation. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/general-purpose-version-1-account-migration-frequently-asked-questions) For Azure Databricks managed storage accounts: If your workspace relies on a GPv1 storage account, you won't be able to migrate that account manually. As part of this retirement, Microsoft will schedule and complete a managed migration of affected accounts to GPv2 on your behalf; no action is required. Azure Databricks accounts will not be part of this migration and will be done separately. When Azure Databricks account migration is planned, notifications will be sent as appropriate. Any non-Azure Databricks accounts that use GPv1 will require manual migration. Automatic migration warning After 13 October 2026, all existing GPv1 storage accounts will be automatically migrated over to a GPv2 account, which may result in higher billing costs. Your decision not to migrate an existing GPv1 storage account will be construed as consent for Microsoft to migrate the account on your behalf. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. (https://learn.microsoft.com/answers/tags/125/azure-blob-storage) If you have a support plan and need technical help, open the Azure portal (https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/HelpAndSupportBlade/overview) and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.

Additionally, on 30 April 2028 AKS will remove Ubuntu 22.04 node images and existing code, causing scaling and remediation operations to fail. Recommended action To avoid service disruptions such as security vulnerabilities, failed node image upgrades, and scaling failures, migrate to Ubuntu 24.04 or later by 30 June 2027. (https://aka.ms/aks/upgrade-os-version)Your migration options include: Default Operating System SKU (OSSku): If you're using 'Ubuntu,' you'll automatically migrate to Ubuntu 24.04 when you upgrade your Kubernetes version to 1.35 or later. Versioned OSSku: If you're using 'Ubuntu2204,' update your OSSku to 'Ubuntu' for Kubernetes 1.35 or later, or 'Ubuntu2404' for Kubernetes 1.32 or later. short_description_solution: Action required: Validate Java TLS compatibility before App Service JDK security updates (starting 20 October 2026)
summary: You’re receiving this notification because one or more of your Azure subscriptions use Java workloads on Azure App Service.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because one or more of your Azure subscriptions use Java workloads on Azure App Service. Starting on 20 October 2026 (phased rollout), App Service Java runtimes may begin updating to JDK 11.0.30+, 17.0.18+, and 21.0.10+ (and later patch versions) during region-specific maintenance windows/non-business hours. In these JDK versions: SHA-1 is disabled for TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2 handshake signatures. TLS_RSA cipher suites are disabled by default. These changes improve security by removing legacy cryptographic algorithms, but they can cause compatibility issues with older endpoints or dependencies. For production workloads, Microsoft guidance remains to use pinned patch JVM versions to reduce unanticipated outages from patch auto-update: Deploy and Configure Tomcat, JBoss EAP, or Java SE Apps - Azure App Service | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/configure-language-java-deploy-run?tabs=windows&pivot%E2%80%A6) Potential impact Applications that depend on legacy TLS settings may experience connection failures, commonly seen as SSLHandshakeException in application logs (often not platform logs), including: "No appropriate protocol (protocol is disabled or cipher suites are inappropriate)"This usually indicates the remote endpoint only supports TLSRSA cipher suites. "No supported signature algorithm..."This usually indicates the remote endpoint signs TLS 1.2 handshakes with SHA-1. Action required 1.Identify impacted connections. Review application logs for SSLHandshakeException. Audit dependencies/endpoints for SHA-1 handshake signatures or TLSRSA-only cipher support. 2.Remediate incompatible dependencies. Update endpoints/libraries to support modern cryptographic settings, such as SHA-256+ signatures and stronger cipher suites. 3.Validate in pre-production. Test compatibility before rollout. For testing environments, set Platform Release Setting to "latest" so runtime changes are exercised early. 4.Use temporary mitigation if needed for production continuity. If remediation cannot complete before rollout, consider pinning to a known-good Java patch version as a short-term mitigation. Track and remove this mitigation once dependencies are updated. 5.Override Java security settings only as a last resort (not recommended long-term). This can reduce cryptographic security posture and should be time-boxed. Create a file named security-override.properties in your site directory (example path shown below): # D:\home\site\security-override.properties jdk.tls.disabledAlgorithms=SSLv3, TLSv1, TLSv1.1, DTLSv1.0, RC4, DES, MD5withRSA, DH keySize less than 1024, EC keySize less than 224, 3DESEDECBC, anon, NULL Then add the following JVM argument to your app's JAVAOPTS: -Djava.security.properties=D:\home\site\security-override.properties Important: Treat this override as temporary. Plan removal after endpoint/dependency remediation. short_description_solution: Action required: Migrate your legacy Azure general-purpose v1 account to a general-purpose v2 account
summary: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that have a GPv1 storage account. For reference, you can find this health advisory notification in the Azure portal using tracking ID: XTKT-BW8.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that have a GPv1 storage account. For reference, you can find this health advisory notification in the Azure portal (https://aka.ms/AzureServiceHealthAdvisories) using tracking ID: XTKT-BW8. From 1 September 2026 the creation of new GPv1 accounts will be blocked, the creation of GPv2 accounts will be unaffected. On 13 October 2026, we'll retire GPv1 storage accounts. To avoid disruptions, migrate your GPv1 storage accounts to GPv2 accounts before that date (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-account-upgrade?tabs=azure-portal). GPv2 accounts give you access to the latest Azure Storage features while providing improved performance and true zonal redundancy support. Recommended action To avoid service disruptions, migrate your GPv1 storage accounts to GPv2 by 13 October 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-account-upgrade?tabs=azure-portal). To view your impacted resources in the Azure portal, go to the Storage Center (https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_StorageHub/StorageHub.MenuView/~/StorageAccountsBrowse)and look for Kind: Storage. For additional ways to access impacted resource information, see this documentation (https://aka.ms/AzureRetirementImpactedResourcesChannels). Watch the recorded video and demo here (https://aka.ms/GPv1RetirementLiveStream). Frequently asked questions are available in the documentation. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/general-purpose-version-1-account-migration-frequently-asked-questions) For Azure Databricks managed storage accounts: If your workspace relies on a GPv1 storage account, you won't be able to migrate that account manually. As part of this retirement, Microsoft will schedule and complete a managed migration of affected accounts to GPv2 on your behalf; no action is required. Azure Databricks accounts will not be part of this migration and will be done separately. When Azure Databricks account migration is planned, notifications will be sent as appropriate. Any non-Azure Databricks accounts that use GPv1 will require manual migration. Automatic migration warning After 13 October 2026, all existing GPv1 storage accounts will be automatically migrated over to a GPv2 account, which may result in higher billing costs. Your decision not to migrate an existing GPv1 storage account will be construed as consent for Microsoft to migrate the account on your behalf. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. (https://learn.microsoft.com/answers/tags/125/azure-blob-storage) If you have a support plan and need technical help, open the Azure portal (https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/HelpAndSupportBlade/overview) and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.

summary: You’re receiving this notification because you’re associated with one or more Azure subscriptions with Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server instances. description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions with Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server instances. For reference, you can find this notification in the Azure portal under Service Health/Health advisories (https://aka.ms/AzureServiceHealthAdvisories) using tracking ID: ZPDZ-SL8. We've rolled out improvements to the high availability experience for Azure Database for PostgreSQL to simplify configuration and strengthen long-term resiliency against zonal failures. What's changing With this experience enabled in the Azure portal and Azure CLI, Azure will now default to zone-redundant high availability. If the selected region doesn't support that, you can choose a fallback mechanism (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/postgresql/high-availability/concepts-high-availability#configure-business-critical-high-availability-options) by selecting the fallback checkbox in the Azure portal or by using the allow-same-zone parameter in the Azure CLI. Changes in the Azure portal include: High availability is now labelled business critical (high availability). If you previously had the experience enabled, no action is required from you. A new zonal resiliency option is available. When enabled, Azure deploys a standby server in a different availability zone from the primary one, helping protect workloads from zonal outages. Automatic migration notice Automatic migration will be supported for new servers created after 12 February 2026 as soon as regional capacity is available. Servers created before 12 February 2026 will be automatically migrated over time. You won't need to redeploy or make configuration changes. From 1 September 2026, servers created using same-zone high availability via developer tools including Terraform, Bicep, SDKs (.NET, Python, Java, JavaScript, and Go), PowerShell, and Ansible will be automatically migrated once capacity becomes available in the region. After the transition, writes are committed across multiple availability zones. This may result in minor changes in write behaviour, with minimal latency impact and improved resiliency and durability. If you'd like to migrate sooner, self-service migration options, such as point-in-time restore or read replicas, will allow you to move to a zone-redundant configuration at your own pace. Read our documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/postgresql/high-availability/how-to-configure-high-availability?tabs=portal-enable-existing-server%2Cportal-disable-existing-server%2Cportal-enable-new-server%2Cportal-forced-failover%2Cportal-planned-failover#limitations-and-considerations) to learn more about self-service migration options, zonal resiliency, the built-in fallback capability, and automatic migration behaviour. Help and support If you have questions about how these changes apply to your deployments or automation workflows, please reach out to us through Microsoft support, your account team, or the feedback forum. For reference, you can find this notification in the Azure portal under Service Health/Health advisories (https://aka.ms/AzureServiceHealthAdvisories) using tracking ID: ZPDZ-SL8. We've rolled out improvements to the high availability experience for Azure Database for PostgreSQL to simplify configuration and strengthen long-term resiliency against zonal failures. What's changing With this experience enabled in the Azure portal and Azure CLI, Azure will now default to zone-redundant high availability. If the selected region doesn't support that, you can choose a fallback mechanism (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/postgresql/high-availability/concepts-high-availability#configure-business-critical-high-availability-options) by selecting the fallback checkbox in the Azure portal or by using the allow-same-zone parameter in the Azure CLI. Changes in the Azure portal include: High availability is now labelled business critical (high availability). If you previously had the experience enabled, no action is required from you. A new zonal resiliency option is available. When enabled, Azure deploys a standby server in a different availability zone from the primary one, helping protect workloads from zonal outages. Automatic migration notice Automatic migration will be supported for new servers created after 12 February 2026 as soon as regional capacity is available. Servers created before 12 February 2026 will be automatically migrated over time. You won't need to redeploy or make configuration changes. From 1 September 2026, servers created using same-zone high availability via developer tools including Terraform, Bicep, SDKs (.NET, Python, Java, JavaScript, and Go), PowerShell, and Ansible will be automatically migrated once capacity becomes available in the region. After the transition, writes are committed across multiple availability zones. This may result in minor changes in write behaviour, with minimal latency impact and improved resiliency and durability. If you'd like to migrate sooner, self-service migration options, such as point-in-time restore or read replicas, will allow you to move to a zone-redundant configuration at your own pace. Read our documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/postgresql/high-availability/how-to-configure-high-availability?tabs=portal-enable-existing-server%2Cportal-disable-existing-server%2Cportal-enable-new-server%2Cportal-forced-failover%2Cportal-planned-failover#limitations-and-considerations) to learn more about self-service migration options, zonal resiliency, the built-in fallback capability, and automatic migration behaviour. description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that have a GPv1 storage account. For reference, you can find this health advisory notification in the Azure portal (https://aka.ms/AzureServiceHealthAdvisories) using tracking ID: XTKT-BW8. From 1 September 2026 the creation of new GPv1 accounts will be blocked, the creation of GPv2 accounts will be unaffected. On 13 October 2026, we'll retire GPv1 storage accounts. To avoid disruptions, migrate your GPv1 storage accounts to GPv2 accounts before that date (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-account-upgrade?tabs=azure-portal). GPv2 accounts give you access to the latest Azure Storage features while providing improved performance and true zonal redundancy support. Recommended action To avoid service disruptions, migrate your GPv1 storage accounts to GPv2 by 13 October 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-account-upgrade?tabs=azure-portal). To view your impacted resources in the Azure portal, go to the Storage Center (https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_StorageHub/StorageHub.MenuView/~/StorageAccountsBrowse)and look for Kind: Storage. For additional ways to access impacted resource information, see this documentation (https://aka.ms/AzureRetirementImpactedResourcesChannels). Watch the recorded video and demo here (https://aka.ms/GPv1RetirementLiveStream). Frequently asked questions are available in the documentation. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/general-purpose-version-1-account-migration-frequently-asked-questions) For Azure Databricks managed storage accounts: If your workspace relies on a GPv1 storage account, you won't be able to migrate that account manually. As part of this retirement, Microsoft will schedule and complete a managed migration of affected accounts to GPv2 on your behalf; no action is required. Azure Databricks accounts will not be part of this migration and will be done separately. When Azure Databricks account migration is planned, notifications will be sent as appropriate. Any non-Azure Databricks accounts that use GPv1 will require manual migration. Automatic migration warning After 13 October 2026, all existing GPv1 storage accounts will be automatically migrated over to a GPv2 account, which may result in higher billing costs. Your decision not to migrate an existing GPv1 storage account will be construed as consent for Microsoft to migrate the account on your behalf. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. (https://learn.microsoft.com/answers/tags/125/azure-blob-storage) If you have a support plan and need technical help, open the Azure portal (https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/HelpAndSupportBlade/overview) and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.

short_description_solution: Retirement notice: Ensure your resources that interact with Azure Functions are using TLS 1.2 or later before 31 May 2027
summary: You're receiving this notice because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions using Azure Functions resources that still allow TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1.
description_problem: You're receiving this notice because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions using Azure Functions resources that still allow TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1. To enhance security and provide best-in-class encryption for your data, we'll require all connections to Azure Functions to be secured using Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 or later beginning 31 May 2027. If you have Azure Functions resources that still allow incoming traffic using TLS 1.0 or 1.1, you'll need to transition them to only allow TLS 1.2 or later (https://aka.ms/tls-deprecation-appservice/config) before that date. Before making configuration changes, you'll need to confirm that all apps, services, and dependencies connecting to your resources support TLS 1.2 or later. Enforcing TLS 1.2 without validation may cause service disruptions. While the Microsoft implementation of older TLS versions is not known to have vulnerabilities, TLS 1.2 and later versions provide improved security features, including perfect forward secrecy and stronger cipher suites. Recommended action To avoid potential service disruptions, set the minimum TLS version of your Azure Functions resources to 1.2 or later (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/tls-minimum-version?tabs=portal#update-your-minimum-tls-version) before 31 May 2027. Before setting the minimum TLS version, check whether your Azure Functions resources are receiving traffic over TLS 1.0 or 1.1 (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/tls-minimum-version?tabs=portal#check-for-tls-10-and-11-traffic). You can view your affected resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook (https://aka.ms/ServicesRetirementWorkbook). Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://aka.ms/tls-deprecation-functions/qa). If you have a support plan and need technical help, create a support request (https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/HelpAndSupportBlade/overview).

short_description_solution: Retirement notice: We're improving the high availability experience for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
summary: You’re receiving this notification because you’re associated with one or more Azure subscriptions with Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server instances. For reference, you can find this notification in the Azure portal under Service Health/Health advisories using tracking ID: ZPDZ-SL8.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions with Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server instances. For reference, you can find this notification in the Azure portal under Service Health/Health advisories (https://aka.ms/AzureServiceHealthAdvisories) using tracking ID: ZPDZ-SL8. We've rolled out improvements to the high availability experience for Azure Database for PostgreSQL to simplify configuration and strengthen long-term resiliency against zonal failures. What's changing With this experience enabled in the Azure portal and Azure CLI, Azure will now default to zone-redundant high availability. If the selected region doesn't support that, you can choose a fallback mechanism (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/postgresql/high-availability/concepts-high-availability#configure-business-critical-high-availability-options) by selecting the fallback checkbox in the Azure portal or by using the allow-same-zone parameter in the Azure CLI. Changes in the Azure portal include: High availability is now labelled business critical (high availability). If you previously had the experience enabled, no action is required from you. A new zonal resiliency option is available. When enabled, Azure deploys a standby server in a different availability zone from the primary one, helping protect workloads from zonal outages. Automatic migration notice Automatic migration will be supported for new servers created after 12 February 2026 as soon as regional capacity is available. Servers created before 12 February 2026 will be automatically migrated over time. You won't need to redeploy or make configuration changes. From 1 September 2026, servers created using same-zone high availability via developer tools including Terraform, Bicep, SDKs (.NET, Python, Java, JavaScript, and Go), PowerShell, and Ansible will be automatically migrated once capacity becomes available in the region. After the transition, writes are committed across multiple availability zones. This may result in minor changes in write behaviour, with minimal latency impact and improved resiliency and durability. If you'd like to migrate sooner, self-service migration options, such as point-in-time restore or read replicas, will allow you to move to a zone-redundant configuration at your own pace. Read our documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/postgresql/high-availability/how-to-configure-high-availability?tabs=portal-enable-existing-server%2Cportal-disable-existing-server%2Cportal-enable-new-server%2Cportal-forced-failover%2Cportal-planned-failover#limitations-and-considerations) to learn more about self-service migration options, zonal resiliency, the built-in fallback capability, and automatic migration behaviour. Help and support If you have questions about how these changes apply to your deployments or automation workflows, please reach out to us through Microsoft support, your account team, or the feedback forum. short_description_solution: Action required: Verify your OS compatibility with Microsoft Azure Network Adapter (MANA) hardware for Intel D- and E- v5-series VMs and Cobalt 100 D- and E- v6-series VMs
summary: You're receiving this notification because you're running one or more Azure virtual machine workloads that may be affected by an upcoming infrastructure change.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're running one or more Azure virtual machine workloads that may be affected by an upcoming infrastructure change. As previously communicated, starting on 26 May 2026, Azure may begin deploying the following virtual machines (VMs) on Microsoft Azure Network Adapter (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-overview)-enabled hardware in limited regions: Intel: Dsv5, Dv5, Ddsv5, Ddv5, Dlsv5, Dldsv5, Esv5, Ev5, Edsv5, Edv5, Ebsv5, Ebdsv5 Cobalt 100: Dpsv6, Dpdsv6, Dplsv6, Dpldsv6, Epsv6, Epdsv6 The regional deployments schedule previously communicated is: 26 May 2026 - West Central US 27 May 2026 - East Asia 28 May 2026 - Norway West 29 May 2026 - Spain Central Service Health notifications will continue when there are additional regions to announce. If you're running the above listed VMs using Accelerated Networking, any new VM deployments or existing VMs which are redeployed due to maintenance events or customer action may land on MANA-compatible hardware once it's live in your region. If your VMs are Network Virtual Appliance (NVA) workloads, you'll need to verify that they're compatible with MANA-enabled hardware before 28 May 2026. Verifying compatibility can help mitigate potential networking performance degradation, while also allowing your workloads to take full advantage of the enhanced networking performance provided by MANA-enabled hardware. If you don't use Accelerated Networking with the above VMs or are running a supported Windows OS version (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-overview?tabs=NetworkManager) on these VMs, no further action is required. Required action Verify that your workloads are compatible with MANA-enabled hardware by following the steps below before 28 May 2026: Identify all Intel D- and E- v5-series and Cobalt 100 D- and E- v6-series VMs using Accelerated Networking running NVA workloads. Verify your Linux OS is MANA compatible. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-linux) If your OS isn't MANA compatible, upgrade to an OS or NVA product that is. Contact your NVA provider for a list of MANA compatible products. If you have NVA workloads and need additional time to complete step 3, you can receive a temporary MANA exception by applying and enabling the "LegacyVMNVA" tag (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-network-virtual-appliance-opt-out#temporary-mana-exception-with-legacyvmnva). This exception will expire on 31 May 2027. If the "LegacyVMNV" tag isn't applied and enabled before your region has the MANA-enabled hardware, your VMs may be deployed on that hardware. Upgrade to a MANA compatible OS or NVA product by 31 May 2027. After that date, any VM could land on MANA-enabled hardware. If you continue using Intel v5 or Cobalt 100 VM sizes without MANA compatibility, they'll remain supported on both existing Mellanox and new MANAenabled hardware until the size is retired. However, you may experience network performance degradation. Help and support If you have questions or run into any issues, please contact your Customer Support Account Manager (CSAM), if available, or reach out to Support (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-machines/vm-support-help) for assistance. The following resources are available to support you: Microsoft Azure Network Adapter overview (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-overview) MANA support for existing VM sizes (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-existing-sizes) MANA support for Network Virtual Appliances (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-network-virtual-appliance-opt-out) Windows VMs with the Microsoft Azure Network Adapter (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/accelerated-networking-mana-windows#verify-that-traffic-is-flowing-through-mana) Support (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-machines/vm-support-help)

description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you have one or more Azure subscriptions currently using legacy authentication in Azure Monitor Container Insights. Recommended action To avoid disruptions, migrate from legacy to managed identity authentication before 30 September 2026. Read our documentation (https://aka.ms/CILegacyAuthMigration) to learn how to migrate your Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters with a single click in the Azure portal. You'll also find command line options and a bulk migration script. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://learn.microsoft.com/answers/tags/20/azure-monitor). If you have a support plan and need technical help, please create a support request (https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/HelpAndSupportBlade/newsupportrequest). Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook (https://aka.ms/ServicesRetirementWorkbook). summary: You’re receiving this notification because you’re associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Ubuntu 22.04 for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters. For reference, you can find this notification in the Azure portal under Service Health/Health advisories using tracking ID: 9Y2Z-_K8.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Ubuntu 22.04 for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters. For reference, you can find this notification in the Azure portal under Service Health/Health advisories using tracking ID: 9Y2Z-_K8. On 30 June 2027, we'll retire Ubuntu 22.04 on Azure Kubernetes Service. To avoid disruptions, transition to Ubuntu 24.04 or later by that date. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/upgrade-os-version) (https://aka.ms/aks/supported-ubuntu-versions)Newer supported versions include kernel updates and security improvements (https://discourse.ubuntu.com/t/ubuntu-24-04-lts-noble-numbat-release-notes/39890). Between now and 30 June 2027, you can continue to use Ubuntu 22.04 on AKS without disruption. If you don't migrate by 30 June 2027, you won't be able to create new node pools, AKS won't produce new node images, and you'll no longer receive security patches for existing node pools. If you'd like to enable long-term support with Kubernetes version 1.33 or later, first update your node pools to Ubuntu 24.04. Additionally, on 30 April 2028 AKS will remove Ubuntu 22.04 node images and existing code, causing scaling and remediation operations to fail. Recommended action To avoid service disruptions such as security vulnerabilities, failed node image upgrades, and scaling failures, migrate to Ubuntu 24.04 or later by 30 June 2027. (https://aka.ms/aks/upgrade-os-version)Your migration options include: Default Operating System SKU (OSSku): If you're using 'Ubuntu,' you'll automatically migrate to Ubuntu 24.04 when you upgrade your Kubernetes version to 1.35 or later. Versioned OSSku: If you're using 'Ubuntu2204,' update your OSSku to 'Ubuntu' for Kubernetes 1.35 or later, or 'Ubuntu2404' for Kubernetes 1.32 or later. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://learn.microsoft.com/answers/tags/200/azure-kubernetes-service) or AKS GitHub. If you have a support plan and need technical help, follow our documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-portal/supportability/how-to-create-azure-support-request#open-a-support-request-from-the-global-header) to create a support request. Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook (https://aka.ms/ServicesRetirementWorkbook). Please note that retirements may not be visible in the workbook for up to two weeks after being announced.
